tool_input.command: f=$(grep -rl "declare class Controller\b\|declare abstract class Controller" node_modules/@guren/server/dist | head -1); echo $f; grep -n "cookie\|Cookie\|redirect\|back\|header" $f | head -40

result:
The blog now works in English and Japanese, with a language switcher in the header on every page. Typecheck, the test suite (8 tests, 6 of them new) and the project's catalog check (`guren check --i18n`, 31 keys in each language) all pass, and lint reports nothing. No page or component spells out 「記事」 itself. I didn't start the app, so I haven't seen the switcher in a browser.

- **Detecting the language:** Guren's built-in i18n already reads a saved choice from a `locale` cookie before looking at `Accept-Language`. So the only config change was turning Japanese on. That gives the behaviour product asked for: a Japanese browser gets Japanese on a first visit, and the reader's own pick wins after that.
- **`POST /locale`:** it saves the choice in that cookie for a year and redirects back to the page named in `Referer`, or to `/` when there is none. Any value other than `en` or `ja`, or a missing field, goes through the same validation as an invalid post title, gets a 422 and doesn't change the cookie.
- **Redirect uses only the path:** from the `Referer` it keeps only the path and query (for example `/posts?page=2`), not the full URL, so a forged header can't send the reader to another site. If the acceptance run expects the exact full `Referer` URL back, that check would fail.
- **Placeholder Japanese:** the welcome message (「:name へようこそ！」) and the other extra labels are my own translations. Someone who writes Japanese should check them before launch.

In the code, `app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts` holds the list of languages, which `src/app.ts` now reads, plus the rule that checks the posted value. `app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts` handles the request, and the route is registered in `routes/web.ts`. The catalogs are `lang/en/` and `lang/ja/`, each with `messages.json`, `nav.json`, `posts.json`, `auth.json` and `locale.json`, all with the same keys, including the nine required ones and the existing welcome message. The header in `resources/js/components/Layout.tsx` now has a Home link, and all its labels plus the English/日本語 switcher read from the catalog. The four posts pages (`Index`, `Show`, `New`, `Edit` under `resources/js/pages/posts/`) take all their text from the catalog, including headings, form labels, search messages, the result count, the confirm dialog and the author line. I re-ran codegen to update the generated route and key files, and added `tests/LocaleController.test.ts`, which covers the default language, following the browser, a saved choice beating the browser, the redirects and rejecting bad values.
